compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX 5090M sm_100, 82 SMs, 32 KiB groupshared cap in DXIL path. Tensor cores not directly available in HLSL cs_6_8 (no WMMA in DXIL standard path). FP16 math via float16_t.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Per-window work is tiny (16 tokens x 32 channels). Most ops are dominated by elementwise + small matmuls. Compute is modest; memory traffic and launch overhead dominate.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Without tensor cores accessible in HLSL, FP16 MAD throughput is bound by vector ALU. Still plenty for this workload.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input: 1*720*1280*32 fp16 = ~58 MB. Output: same ~58 MB. Weights tiny (~22 KB total). With full fusion, each input element streamed once -> ~116 MB R+W = ~130 us at 896 GB/s lower bound.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Naive multi-pass implementation would multiply traffic 5-10x; full fusion essential.

register_pressure.notes: Per window: 16 tokens * 32 ch = 512 fp16 values = 256 dwords. Q,K,V each 16*32=512 -> manageable. Hidden MLP 16*128=2048 fp16 = 1024 dwords; large but tractable if distributed across threads.
register_pressure.risk: If a single thread holds an entire window, register spill is likely. Need to distribute across threads in a group.

nodes.notes: SUMMARY: Swin block on (1,720,1280,32) fp16, window=4x4, single head, no shift, dim=32, hidden=128. Independent units = 180*320=57600 windows, each window = 16 tokens of 32 channels. PHASES per window: LN1 -> QKV(32->96) -> Q*K^T scaled (16x16) + rpe_bias -> softmax -> attn@V (16x32) -> proj(32->32) + residual -> LN2 -> fc1(32->128) -> GELU -> fc2(128->32) + residual. CLASSIFICATION: fused attention+MLP block, small per-window working set, embarrassingly parallel across windows. DEPENDENCIES: LN reduces over C=32; QK reduces over C=32; softmax reduces over N=16; attn@V reduces over N=16; FC reduces over 32/128. All reductions are small. WORKING SET per window in fp16: input 16*32=512, Q/K/V 3*16*32=1536, attn 16*16=256, post-attn 16*32=512, MLP hidden 16*128=2048, output 16*32=512. Total ~5.3K fp16 = 10.6 KiB - fits comfortably in 32 KiB groupshared per group. WEIGHTS total: qkv 3072 + proj 1024 + fc1 4096 + fc2 4096 + biases ~288 + LN params 128 = ~12.7 KiB fp16. Fits in shared too. REGIMES: (a) bandwidth-bound full-fusion: ~130us lower bound; (b) compute-bound if poor reuse: small mats favor thread-cooperative gemm; (c) latency-bound if too few groups: 57600 windows >> 82 SMs * occupancy so fine. DESIGN: 1 threadgroup per window, 64 threads (2 warps) cooperating. Stage input window + LN -> registers, do QKV via cooperative matmul, write Q,K,V to groupshared, compute attn 16x16 in registers, softmax via wave reductions, attn@V, proj+residual, LN2, fc1+GELU, fc2+residual all in shared/registers, write output. Weights can be loaded once per group from SRV (cached in L2 across groups). KNOBS: threads/group (32/64/128), where to stage Q/K/V (shared vs reg), whether to preload weights to shared, vectorization (float16_t4 loads via Buffer<uint2> reinterpret).

action.description: Implement a single-dispatch fully-fused HLSL compute shader: one threadgroup per 4x4 window. Threads cooperatively load the 16x32 fp16 window, perform LN1, QKV projection, Q*K^T + rpe + softmax, attn@V, proj+residual, LN2, fc1+GELU, fc2+residual, and write output. Use groupshared for tokens, Q/K/V, attn matrix; keep weights read from SRV (L2-cached) or staged once at group entry. Dispatch grid = (320,180,1) windows.
action.rationale: Full fusion eliminates 5-10x global memory round-trips between phases. Per-window working set (~10 KiB activations) easily fits in 32 KiB groupshared. With 57600 windows >> 82 SMs, occupancy is saturated. Estimated lower bound ~130 us bandwidth-bound.
action.title: Fully-fused single-kernel per-window threadgroup

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: 32 KiB groupshared cap respected (~10-15 KiB used). 82 SMs * 2048 threads = 167K threads available; 57600 groups * 64 threads scales well.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Small matmuls (16x32x32, 16x32x128) map well to wave-cooperative dot products. No tensor core required.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Need careful thread mapping to keep all 64 threads busy across phases with different shapes.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Single read of input, single write of output. Weights ~13 KiB fit in L2 trivially, shared across all groups.
memory_bandwidth.risk: None significant - this is the bandwidth-optimal structure.

register_pressure.notes: Per-thread holds small tile fragments; bulk lives in shared. Should stay under 64 registers/thread enabling >=8 groups/SM.
register_pressure.risk: MLP hidden=128 phase may inflate regs if not split across threads carefully.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: This is the baseline strong candidate. Alternatives below differ in thread-count and weight-staging strategy and cannot coexist with this exact configuration.

action.description: Like the fused per-window plan, but pack multiple windows (e.g., 4 or 8) per threadgroup to amortize weight-load cost and raise arithmetic per group. Each group processes a small tile of windows with shared weight staging in groupshared memory.
action.rationale: Weights are constant across all windows. Loading them once into shared memory per group and processing several windows boosts reuse. Reduces total weight reads from SRV though L2 already absorbs most of this.
action.title: Multi-window-per-group with shared weight staging

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Working set scales linearly with windows-per-group; 4 windows ~40 KiB exceeds 32 KiB cap. Likely cap at 2 windows or stream weights.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: May exceed 32 KiB shared limit; reduces total group count which is already plenty.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Marginal: weights are small enough that L2 likely already absorbs them in the simpler design.

register_pressure.notes: Higher per-group state; may pressure registers per thread.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: Alternative to single-window-per-group; cannot run simultaneously because group dimensioning differs. Tradeoff: more reuse vs tighter shared budget.

action.description: Reorganize the per-window plan so that each thread owns one full token (16 threads per window, possibly with multiple windows per group to fill a warp). Each thread holds its own 32-element vector in registers across LN1, QKV, attention output accumulation, LN2, FC1 hidden vector (128 elems split), and FC2 output. Use wave intrinsics for cross-token reductions (LN means, softmax max/sum, attn dot products).
action.rationale: Maps naturally to a warp: 16 threads = 16 tokens. Wave intrinsics (WaveActiveSum, WaveReadLaneAt) replace groupshared reductions, minimizing barriers. Each warp can handle 2 windows (32 lanes / 16 tokens) for full warp utilization.
action.title: Token-per-thread mapping using wave intrinsics for reductions

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX 5090 warp size 32. Two windows per warp keeps all lanes busy. FC1 hidden=128 per token requires 128 fp16 = 64 dwords in registers per thread - acceptable.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Excellent fit for wave size and small token count.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: FC1 hidden vector may push register count; could split into two passes.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Same single-pass streaming as fused plan. Weights broadcast via wave reads from groupshared after one-time load.

register_pressure.notes: Per-thread: input 32, Q 32, K 32 (only read from shared), V 32, hidden 128 (only during MLP), output 32 -> peak ~200 fp16 = 100 dwords. Within 255 register budget.
register_pressure.risk: Tight during MLP phase; may need to spill hidden to shared.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: Distinct from per-window cooperative because thread granularity is one full token vs sub-token tiles. Reductions use wave intrinsics instead of groupshared+barrier, fewer syncs.

kernel_summary: Fused Swin transformer block over a (1,720,1280,32) fp16 feature map with 4x4 non-overlapping windows, single head, no shift, dim=32, MLP hidden=128. Computation per window (16 tokens, 32 channels): LN1, QKV linear, scaled Q*K^T + relative position bias, softmax, attn@V, output proj + residual, LN2, FC1, GELU, FC2 + residual. 57,600 independent windows provide massive parallelism. Per-window activation working set (~10 KiB fp16) and all weights (~13 KiB fp16) fit easily within the 32 KiB groupshared cap, making full single-kernel fusion the dominant strategy. Bottleneck is global memory bandwidth (~116 MB R+W, ~130us lower bound on 896 GB/s). Key constraints: cs_6_8 (no DXIL WMMA), 32 KiB shared cap, single dispatch, weights as SRVs t1-t13, output as UAV u0.
open_questions: Does cs_6_8 in this runner support float16_t arithmetic natively, or will it be promoted to fp32 in DXIL (affecting register footprint and throughput)?
Are wave intrinsics (WaveActiveSum, WaveReadLaneAt) fully available and performant in this DXIL path on Blackwell?
How aggressively should weights be staged into groupshared vs left in SRV/L2? L2 is 64 MB and weights are 13 KiB so L2 likely suffices.
Optimal threadgroup size: 32 (single warp, one window), 64 (two warps), or 128 (handle multiple windows)?
Is GELU using the exact erf formulation or the tanh approximation in the reference's fp16 path? Need to match within rtol=0.01.
Does LayerNorm's fp32 internal accumulation matter for tolerance at dim=32, or is fp16 accumulation sufficient?
Best layout for Q/K/V in groupshared to avoid bank conflicts during 16x32 * 32x16 matmul and 16x16 * 16x32 matmul?
Should the RPE bias (256 fp16) be preloaded into groupshared/registers once per group, or read directly from SRV (likely L1-cached)?
